item.title: dictionary
item.description:
CiiaKua

Used to describe certain characteristics of water. It has different meanings in different contexts: in 0xA3 it is a sentence Nishimiya scolded when interrupting the audience; in 0xA9 it is Kate scolding you, referring to muddy sewage.

The pronunciation is similar to “watermelon” in Mandarin Chinese.

Classical Latin: /ki.ja.kwa/

Ecclesiastical Latin: /tʃi.ja.kwa/

Italian: /ˈtʃja.kwa/ or /ˈtʃi.a.kwa/

Spanish-Latin American accent: /ˈsja.kwa/

Spain-Mainland: /ˈθja.kwa/

French: /si.a.ky.a/ or /si.a.ku.a/

Portuguese: /ˈsja.kwa/

Husburd

In 0x07 refers to the former head of the family. Pronounced /ˈhʊs.bʊrd/ according to the Germanic languages ​​of ancient Norse and England.
